subject: Re: Acme - Concurrency & Rate Limits follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme - Concurrency & Rate Limits follow-up (post-demo)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Latency SLOs: you said 95th p95 token latency target of ~120ms for short-form generation (<=256 tokens) and ~250ms for streaming long-form.
- Throughput: expected sustained throughput of ~40k tokens/sec during business hours, spiking to ~120k tokens/sec during peak batch jobs.
- Concurrency: ~1,200 parallel requests from your connection pool (mix of single-turn text gen + streaming chat).
- Streaming requirements: client needs chunked streaming with keep-alive connections; each connection may multiplex up to 6 concurrent streams.

We still need the CSV you mentioned with per-endpoint QPS and average payload sizes — that will help us map to batching and KV cache recommendations. Attaching the template we use ("acme_concurrency_requirements.xlsx").

Next steps:
1) You to fill and return the XLSX by Tuesday EOD.
2) We'll run a quick capacity sketch and propose a concurrency/quota tier + fallback strategy (regional routing + burst pool) by Thursday.
3) If the sketch looks good, we can convert to a committed Dedicated tier quote for predictable SLOs.

Two notes on constraints: Redwood imposes per-connection rate limits and an account-level concurrency quota. We can flex the account-level quota for committed customers; per-connection limits (to protect routing fairness) are configurable within a safe window.

Happy to jump on a quick call with Eng if that helps.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — great demo. I've filled the first tab of your template and attached; still need to double-check a couple of traffic-shape assumptions with the infra team.

A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 1,200 parallel requests is an upper bound across our fleet; typical steady-state is ~400.
- For streaming, most sessions are short (1–2 minutes) but a small subset of analytics jobs stream for up to 20 minutes.
- We will likely use two regions (us-east, us-west) for redundancy.

On limits: we can commit to a 12-month consumption MIN if that helps with quota increases, but we need a clear fallback plan if we hit account throttling during peaks.

I'll return the completed sheet by EOD tomorrow.

—Jordan
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme - Concurrency & Rate Limits follow-up — quota ask

Forwarding Jordan's responses — looks like Acme is willing to commit if we can guarantee a fallback policy and a decent committed-min for the quota bump. Key asks:

- Account-level concurrency target: support up to 1,200 parallel requests across regions with burst to 2,500 for <10 min windows.
- Per-connection limits: want to be able to multiplex up to 6 streams per TCP connection (they use connection pooling).
- Streaming SLO: p95 chunk latency <= 250ms with stable keep-alives.

Logan — can you sketch whether we can support 1,200 steady and short bursts to 2.5k with our Dedicated infra without impacting existing Dedicated customers? If not, what's the alternative (regional burst pool + throttling policy)?

I'll patch together a short SLA language we can present for the committed-min + quota bump.

Thanks —Marissa
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme - Concurrency & Rate Limits follow-up — quota ask

Marissa/Laura — quick assessment:

- Steady 1,200 parallel requests: doable on Dedicated with an allocation of 3 x A100-style pools (or equivalent) assuming average request size is ~120 tokens/req. We'll need to reserve capacity and update routing weights.
- Short bursts to 2,500: feasible if we provide a regional burst pool (shared) with preemptible capacity and a short-lived priority queue. We should model a backpressure policy: degrade non-critical routes and spin up burst nodes for 10–15 minute windows.
- Per-connection multiplexing: supported at the proxy layer; need to ensure token rate per-connection cap is relaxed for Acme's tenant and monitored.
- Streaming p95 <=250ms: likely achievable but depends on their end-to-end network; recommend a small pilot to measure client-side network jitter.

Action items:
1) I'll put together a capacity sketch and a proposed quota table (steady vs. burst vs. emergency) by Thursday.
2) Laura — can you draft SLA language that ties committed-min to a guaranteed account-level concurrency and a documented fallback plan?

If Acme is willing to sign a 12-month committed-min, we can offer a 25% discount on Dedicated capacity and raise the account-level concurrency quota accordingly.

—Logan
Senior Infra PM
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lowe <jordan.lowe@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed SLA language & next steps — Acme concurrency quota

Hi Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround on the sheet. We reviewed your numbers and sketched a proposal:

Summary proposal:
- Steady account concurrency quota: 1,200 parallel requests across us-east/us-west.
- Burst allowance: up to 2,500 concurrent requests for up to 10 minutes per hour, subject to a regional burst pool.
- Per-connection multiplexing: allow up to 6 streams/connection and increase per-connection token rate cap to accommodate their pool.
- Streaming SLO: Redwood will target p95 chunk latency <= 250ms and will execute a 2-week pilot to baseline client-side behavior.
- Fallback policy: if account-level throttling occurs, Redwood will (a) automatically route to secondary region, (b) enable reduced-quality (quantized) model variants for non-critical routes, and (c) notify Acme with a mitigation timeline.

Commercials:
- 12-month committed-min (prepay or monthly commitment) to be defined; proposed 25% discount on Dedicated capacity for the committed term.
- Addendum will include quota bump and SLA language; implementation timeline estimated 2–3 weeks after contract signature for capacity reservation and routing changes.

Next steps:
1) Jordan — confirm that the proposal aligns with your expectations and that your legal/procurement teams are ok to review an SLA addendum.
2) Marissa/Logan — we'll draft the SLA addendum and the capacity quote; I'll include the pilot plan as an appendix.

Attachment: redwood-sla-draft.pdf (SLA draft)

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of GTM Ops
Redwood Inference
